+# PR190 뒤의 15번째 노트 annotation guard
+
+이 변경은 법규·독립 감사 실적이나 게시 승인이 없는 release-gate engineering이다.
+기준은 PR190의 실제 main merge **`f8ec04a028e38288aa9cbf539fa12244f2cd49a4`**다.
+Root는 corrected candidate `205c8feb08e463fac30c8162a124875befa0ae62`와
+tree `0d0eac7ee844f6db721041d9764b26c8acd1bde1`이 같음을 확인했다. 이 guard는
+공개 origin의 바이트 대조나 게시 검증 승인을 제공하지 않는다. 이후 실제 원본이
+다르면 root가 다시 확보해 명시적으로 재결박·검사해야 한다.
+`annotation_inputs_ready`는 source 결박의 준비 상태이며 게시 승인이 아니다.
+
+고정 원본은 다음과 같다.
+
+- `revisions/baselines/complete-notes-pr190.md`:
+  `c3bd223ff1774917388986a3b4a4e46b2f995e9d702d671309edeb92dd489d16`
+- `revisions/baselines/notes-build-pr190.json`:
+  `d23f20169980cb5c94b24624776f652a233ff3e992c7e91fb940d3edfe8b419b`
+- 14번째 `protected-migration-independent-notes-wave3.json`은 main의 정확한 원바이트
+  `53537abd57b56bc8a839901a766de916c7a06b4275beba8bd2ebf435adf0353e`로 복원한다.
+  현재 export를 통과시키려고 이 parent의 `new_sha256`을 다시 바꾸지 않는다.
+
+새 manifest는 `revisions/notes/protected-migration-after190.json`이며,
+`scripts/notes_after190_annotation.py`가 명시적으로 준비·검증한다. 범위는 한 export와
+그 build metadata뿐이다. 원래 M semantic
+`e1519c0290ff220eb8251307e26340d76d394a7ec1f3e651194d4495a03f1824`,
+edition, revision provenance와 build의 의미 필드를 PR190와 대조한다. census ledger
+해시와 독립 노트 review progress 이외의 build 변경은 허용하지 않는다.
+
+최종 v4 census, version record, 실제 23번 E3 job의 INTEGRATED 상태와 현재
+report/envelope/source raw SHA를 결박한다. 현재 6,989개는 author enumeration 수이며
+새 author source check나 independent legal audit credit로 바꾸지 않는다. 독립 노트
+consumer가 현재 body/census/claim·원 blocker·실제 controller가 선언한 actor/session과
+source를 다시 검증하고 처리 수·KEEP/HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED를 계산한다. 신원 문자열은
+controller-attested declaration이며 암호학적인 신원 인증이 아니다.
+선택된 32개 census의 path/raw SHA 전체도 controller source
+`e78af1cd5ccdd749c3599aa4f36a217af4d06552`의 고정 map digest와 대조한다.
+claim 수가 같아도 다른 census로 바꿔 `--write`하는 방식으로 범위를 넓힐 수 없다.
+E3 원 envelope에 선언된 42개 artifact를 모두 현재 커밋의 원바이트로 대조한다.
+
+중간 LEASED/pending 23번 결과로 manifest를 준비하면 명시적으로 실패한다.
+추가로 15번째 manifest 자체의 `annotation_inputs_ready`가 false이면 게시 검증은
+실패한다. source 변경 후 옛 pending manifest를 그대로 출시할 수 없다.
+
+이 미출시 15번째 guard의 최종 범위는 다음과 같다. 배정 정의를 고정한 것은
+미래 결과를 인증한 것이 아니다. 실제 원장·원 report·envelope·보존 primary bytes와
+claim/submit/integrate 연결을 현재 HEAD에서 확인한 뒤에만 final manifest를 준비한다.
+
+- Legacy question job1–29와 root가 `804178fd`에 실제 배정한 CURRENT DEFAULT wave9의
+  30–33까지 정확한 sequence/ID/stage/question-hash map. 30–33은 각각40문항이며 실제
+  fresh actor `/root/independent_wave9_a`–`d`도 고정한다. 모두 실제 INTEGRATED여야 한다.
+  Phase7의21–24, wave8의25–28, native 현재ID 세 문항의29와 wave9의160문항을 각각
+  결박한다. QUEUED/LEASED/SUBMITTED 또는 status만 조작한 IG는 실패한다.
+- Notes job1–30의 정확한 ID/unit-binding map과 실제 INTEGRATED 결과. 28–30의 F 작성
+  immutable v2 census 보완도 기존 negative/history를 그대로 검증한다.
+- 오직 하나의31번 `BODY_CORRECTION_REASSESSMENT`: w3-a-3의 R 작성 후보를 root가 새
+  immutable record에 재등록한 정확한 경로·raw SHA·job ID. 원 record, candidate revision,
+  24-claim census, 원26번 parent/report/envelope, mapping, 011 HOLD와019/024의 원 negative는
+  그대로여야 한다. 현재 M 본문·선택6989 census에는 새 후보를 넣지 않는다.
+  QUEUED/LEASED/SUBMITTED/INTEGRATED 어느 상태에서도 inactive/current credit0이며
+  metadata의 `current_review_valid:false`, `LEGAL_HOLD`, review 경고를 요구한다.
+- Author job53의 실제 G 세 문항 current-ID source review와 원63개 static source.
+  기존 consumer의 original52 job/event와 모든 static raw SHA 검사를 유지한다.
+  Author 결과를 독립 감사로 바꾸지 않는다. 원2346 question objects와 추가 native3의
+  archive-only 상태를 보존한다. Allocation의 default298은 before snapshot이다.
+  최종 default 수를298로 강제하지 않는다. 실제 현재 hash에 결박된 부정 finding의
+  명시적 safety hold로만 default를 줄일 수 있으며, 원 hold/history를 보존한다.
+  기존 selection/default-review/archive-warning safety validator로 현재 미보류 negative를
+  차단한다. 새 failed default를 KEEP으로 덮거나 이전298 밖의 ID를 추가할 수 없다.
+
+31의 실제 재등록 record는 `.../w3-a-3-v1/registrations/after-census-v2.json`,
+raw SHA `945e120c2676793b7f6649d0eaa5a3cb4eb22b3f2e85fd56d273331a0730dd1c`,
+job `review-independent-notes-body-4c3229fb7bfb76b6`이다. Root checkpoint847d의 명시적
+재결박이며, 보존 ledger와 현재 ledger를 직접 비교해 target 불변·전체306 body 불변과
+정확히 `[w2-c-12,w3-a-6,w3-a-7]`의 sibling census 차이만 확인한다. 현재 처리 수는
+실제 최신 binding에서 계산한다. 비활성31 때문에 원 current credit 하나가 제외되며,
+이전80을 새 현재 수로 고정하거나 N 활성화를 이미 한 것으로 취급하지 않는다.
+29의 실제 F report/envelope 경로도 실제 통합 후에만 고정했다. Wave9는 실제 runbook의
+`independent-phase9-[a-d]-review.json`과 같은 basename의 `-result.json`만 출력 계약으로
+허용한다. 이는 파일 존재나 review 완료의 증거가 아니다. 그 실제 source raw SHA와
+최종 manifest는 아래의 미공개 wave10 확장을 포함한 모든37 job의 실제 통합과
+known-negative containment 후에만 계산한다.
+미래 IG나 임의 source prefix/추가 job을 허용하지 않는다.
+새 note32/question38/author54는 pending이어도 범위 밖이며 별도 검토가 필요하다.
+기존15 manifest의 old25-job/6985 상태를 현재 source의 final proof로 사용할 수 없다.
+
+### 공개 전 wave10 completion bridge
+
+15는 아직 한 번도 공개하지 않았다. `7ea50249`의 33-job 후보 및 실패한 QA는
+과거 checkpoint로 보존하며 실제 공개 baseline으로 쓰지 않는다. 공개된14의 원
+manifest·MD/build snapshot·기존 decoder는 그대로다. 이 변경은16 body 활성화가 아니다.
+
+실제 `08a417e2e53e83501e2756792cda0168fe4ae8a7`의34–37 할당만 추가한다.
+각40개 whole-record hash와 actual `/root/independent_wave10_[a-d]` actor, 원
+priority-source map digest를 코드에 정확히 결박한다. 총160개 중 할당 당시128개는
+현재 default,32개는 archive였다. 160개 전부 default라고 주장하거나 최종 default
+수를229/298 등으로 강제하지 않는다. 기존33개 job의 ID/hash/actor/원source 검증을
+유지한다. 원1–33의 실제 통합 job 전체 digest도08a의 exact 값으로 고정해 과거
+report/negative/envelope receipt를 함께 재작성하는 우회를 막는다. 새 네 job도
+실제 INTEGRATED event, report와 원 envelope, 전 row/hash,
+primary raw bytes 및 controller-attested provenance를 검증해야 한다.
+
+새 출력 계약은 `independent-phase10-[a-d]-review.json`과 같은 basename의
+`-result.json`이다. 파일명 허용은 파일 존재나 감사 완료의 주장이 아니다.
+QUEUED/LEASED/SUBMITTED나 status-only IG는 manifest 생성을 명시적으로 실패시킨다.
+이전 미공개 manifest의 `annotation_inputs_ready: true`도 이 검사를 건너뛸 수 없다.
+실제37개 source가 커밋되고 기존69개 부정 및 새 실제 부정이 source-bound hold로
+격리된 후에만 root가 새 manifest를 생성·재결박하고 전체 QA를 수행한다.
+
+C36의 실제 source-context 노출 경계는 `MA-RW-0051/0061/0062/0064` 네 개다.
+이 네 row의 `existing_answer_correct: NOT_ASSESSED`, `safe_hold_recommended: true`와
+HOLD 또는 더 강한 MINOR_EDIT/MAJOR_REWRITE/DELETE verdict를 유지해야 한다.
+더 강한 실제 negative를 HOLD로 낮추도록 강제하지 않는다. 원 노출 로그와 잠정40개0 기록은
+history로 보존한다. B40/C나머지36은 실제 fresh primary 판단 대상일 뿐 자동
+YES/PASS가 아니다. 이 annotation은 C4 whole-key credit를 만들거나 기존 negative를
+새 KEEP으로 덮지 않는다. 현재 progress는 current builder와 따로 대조한다.
+
+notes31·author53·census6989·M semantic은 그대로다. private/historical context의
+기존 exact 예외만 유지하며 wave10에 새 예외를 자동 생성하지 않는다. 실제 새
+mismatch가 있으면 원 job/report/origin/raw SHA의 증거부터 확인하고 별도 bounded
+검토를 받아야 한다. runtime 검증에는 HEAD-retained bytes만 필요하며 옛 worker
+Git object를 요구하지 않는다. 이 bridge의 canonical/question/legal 새 credit는0이다.
+
+Canonical Q0012와 연결 SG-CII-LIFECYCLE의 철회는 별도 strict decoder가 담당한다.
+최종15 준비 시 그 decoder와 exact retained cause/metadata-only package가 실제로
+존재하고 검증되어야 한다. Notes annotation이 canonical RELEASED 복귀나 guide VERIFIED
+복귀를 허용하지 않는다. 기존1781 protected inventory·공개14 manifest와 decoder를
+바꾸지 않으며, root가 실제 hotfix를 병합한 뒤 두 경로의 합성 검사를 수행한다.
+
+새 candidate 본문 공개는 이 annotation guard 범위 밖이다. 실제15 출시 snapshot을
+기준으로 root가 별도16번째 body migration을 만들어 검증해야 한다. 이31의 독립
+후보 검토도 활성 본문과 일치하기 전에는 현재 credit를 얻지 않는다.
+
+검증은 먼저 현재 source로 export/build를 메모리에서 재생성하여 manifest의
+예상 바이트와 대조한다. `new_sha256`만 바꿔 임의의 annotation이나 법규 승인을
+삽입할 수 없다. 그 후 export를 정확한 PR190 Markdown으로 decode하고 기존
+14개 guard를 원래 코드·원본·parent hash로 차례로 실행한다. 기존 source·semantic
+보호를 새 annotation으로 우회하지 않는다.
+
+Root의 후속 절차는 다음과 같다.
+
+1. 고정된 실제 PR190 merge와 게시 원본을 확인한다. 다른 원본이면 먼저 재결박한다.
+2. E3/Phase 7 등 실제 통합 source와 checkpoint를 커밋한다.
+3. 기존 재생성 순서로 ledger 및 notes 산출물을 갱신한다. 이 worker는 root/shared
+   generated 파일을 쓰지 않는다.
+4. 최종 ledger/raw source 기준으로 아래 명령을 실행하고 새 15번째 manifest만
+   검토·커밋한다. 14번째와 PR190 snapshot은 그대로 둔다.
+5. protected guard, 전체 재생성 확인, 동결 QA와 CI를 새 tree에서 수행한다.
+
+```sh
+python scripts/notes_after190_annotation.py --write
+python scripts/notes_after190_annotation.py --check
+python scripts/verify_representative_protected.py
+```
+
+`--write`는 제안을 준비할 뿐이며 release 승인이 아니다. 현재 generated 파일이
+그 결박과 다르면 protected guard는 실패한다. 이 guard가 허용하는 semantic 범위를
+넓히거나 이전 manifest를 수정하는 방식으로 해결하지 않는다.
+
+범위 검증:
+
+```sh
+python -m pytest -q tests/test_after190_annotation.py tests/test_emergency_note_activation.py
+```
+
+실제 최종 source가 미완료인 동안 준비된 final manifest가 필요한 integration fixture는
+`NOT_RUN` 사유로 skip한다. 범위·tamper·원14 보존·실제 author source 검증은 별도로 실행한다.
+Skip을 final gate PASS로 보고하지 않는다. Root는 모든 실제 source와15 manifest를 고정한
+tree에서 전체 검증·CI·배포 검사를 다시 수행한다.
+
+## 과거 입력 receipt와 현재 source의 구별
+
+일부 immutable wave9·wave10 report는 읽기 당시의 progress, 운영 runbook, nearest-default

+# Optional remediation and current-default review priority
+
+The existing queue order is unchanged unless `plan` receives
+`--prioritize-remediation-and-default` in the `independent-legacy` stage. The
+existing author FIRST cohort, uncredited-ledger gate, incomplete-wave refusal,
+lease recovery, idempotent submit and sequential evidence-bound integration keep
+their existing behavior.
+
+With the option, eligible ledger IDs are ordered deterministically:
+
+1. The three frozen, source-bound remediation IDs.
+2. Other current default IDs from the publication manifest's hash-bound selection.
+3. The remaining IDs in lexical order.
+
+Eligibility still requires an existing source-review date and no independent
+legacy assessment, and excludes every ID assigned in an earlier job. Missing or
+stale source/ledger/default bindings fail. Jobs already assigned are not changed.
+The selected policy and source SHA bindings are recorded in each new job and its
+PLAN event. A plan made while any prior job is incomplete returns no new jobs.
+

+이 문자열 검사는 법적 의미의 충분성을 인증하지 않는다. 실제 reviewer가 별도로 판단한다.
+등록 시 원 snapshot과 현재 선택 unit 전체가 같고, 나머지 unit 전체와 claim binding의
+fingerprint도 같아야 한다. 이후 다른 명시적 version의 등록까지 과거 snapshot에 묶지는 않는다.
+후보 작성 후 다른 unit의 합법적인 census version이 먼저 선택됐다면 원 record를 덮어쓰거나
+검사를 생략하지 않는다. Root가 최신 inventory를 확인하고 새 immutable registration
+record 경로·ID와 나머지-unit fingerprint를 재결박해야 한다. 원 후보·원 record는 보존한다.
+
+바뀌지 않은 명제의 원 `LEGAL_HOLD`·`SOURCE_BLOCKED`는 finding, blocker,
+원 report SHA, 더 오래된 inherited blockers까지 정확히 `carried_legal_blockers`로 남긴다.
+HOLD는 HOLD로, BLOCKED는 BLOCKED 또는 HOLD로만 제출할 수 있다. 본문 일부가
+바뀌었다는 이유로 다른 명제의 negative를 해소하지 못한다.
+
+실제 수정된 명제의 negative만 `reconsidered_legal_negatives`로 분리한다. 새 독립
+reviewer가 원 negative 전체, 수정 span과 새 명제를 명시적으로 재판단해야 한다.
+같은 body/statement hash에 새 긍정 판정을 붙이는 경로는 없다. 과거 body hash의 재등장과
+과거 negative의 원문 명제를 변경 claim으로 재도입하는 등록도 거부한다. 저자의 source 확인,
+날짜 변경, 저자 census의 COMPLETE 열거 상태는 독립 법규 PASS가 아니다.
+
+## Root와 worker의 순서
+
+1. 저자가 원본 archive, 새 body/census, mapping, 실제 primary retrieval/raw SHA,
+   관련 study/card의 실제 입력·후보 source hashes를 먼저 커밋한다. 새 본문은
+   `notes_revision.PATHS`, active/default notes 또는 published export에 넣지 않는다.
+2. Root는 현재 note wave를 통합한 뒤 원본·새 후보·parent를 확인한다. Read-only preview:
+
+   ```sh
+   python scripts/note_review_queue.py --root /ABS/CONTROLLER preview-body \
+     --record reports/full-corpus-review/body-corrections/UNIT-VERSION/record.json
+   ```
+
+   Preview는 원장·본문·생성물을 쓰지 않으며 `inactive`, `LEGAL_HOLD`,
+   `current_review_valid: false`, `daily_eligible: false`, credit 0을 반환한다.
+
+3. Controller의 기존 root-only checkpoint로 등록하고 원장 바이트를 커밋한다.
+
+   ```sh
+   python scripts/note_review_queue.py --root /ABS/CONTROLLER --actor /root reassess-body \
+     --record reports/full-corpus-review/body-corrections/UNIT-VERSION/record.json
+   ```
+
+   새 `body_reassessments` entry와 한 unit job을 append한다. 같은 경로·바이트 재등록은
+   멱등적이다. 복제 job, 다른 purpose 혼합, 가장 최근 parent가 아닌 등록, 진행 중 wave에
+   무단 추가는 실패한다. 서로 다른 unit의 최초 QUEUED/attempt0 후보는 함께 등록할 수 있다.
+   같은 unit의 다음 body 후보는 이전 후보가 실제 활성 binding이 된 뒤에만 새 parent가 된다.
+
+4. 기존 [독립 notes runbook](INDEPENDENT_NOTES_REVIEW_RUNBOOK.md)의 `claim`, `worktree`,
+   heartbeat/recover, submit, evidence cherry-pick, envelope 원바이트 commit, 순차 integrate를
+   그대로 쓴다. Stage는 `independent-notes`, job purpose는 `BODY_CORRECTION_REASSESSMENT`다.
+   후보 body/census 저자와 원 body/source 저자의 actor/session/instance는 claim할 수 없다.
+   알려지지 않은 별칭은 root가 기존 `--known-author`로 등록한다. 문자열 provenance는
+   실제 controller의 attestation이며 외부 신원 인증을 주장하지 않는다.
+5. Worker는 job이 지정한 inactive revision 전문, 최종 census의 모든 claim, 원 negative와
+   원 omissions, 관련 derived 입력 전체를 직접 읽는다. Active body가 아직 원본인 것은
+   정상이다. Census-only 경로처럼 inactive body를 공개 ledger로 먼저 선택하지 않는다.
+   Worker의 쓰기 범위는 기존 `reports/full-corpus-review/independent-notes/`뿐이다.
+   본문·census·원장·기존 보고서를 worker가 수정하지 않는다.
+
+등록 즉시 old KEEP의 현재 credit를 제거하고 HOLD·daily 제외 경고를 표시한다.
+원 batch의 다른 unit은 그대로다. SUBMITTED는 새 현재 credit가 아니다. INTEGRATED여도
+활성 body+census+claim binding이 후보와 다르면 `candidate_review_valid: true`만 남기고
+`current_review_valid: false`와 안전 HOLD를 유지한다. 이력에는 원 판정·원 body hash를 남긴다.
+활성 binding이 나중에 정확히 일치하면 가장 최근 통합 결과 하나만 현재 처리 수에 반영한다.
+법규 HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED 결과도 처리 coverage이며 legal KEEP나 release 승인이 아니다.
+
+## 새 보고서의 추가 계약
+
+각 unit row는 기존 runbook 필드 외에 다음을 포함한다. 확인하지 않은 항목은 true로 만들지 않는다.
+
+```python
+row['actual_body_sha256'] = job['unit_bindings'][uid]['body_sha256']
+row['reviewed_at'] = '실제 timezone-aware UTC timestamp'
+row['body_correction_review'] = {
+    **job['body_correction_review'],
+    'final_body_read_completely': True,
+    'final_census_read_completely': True,
+    'all_parent_negatives_explicitly_reassessed': True,
+    'all_parent_omissions_explicitly_reassessed': True,
+    'all_derived_inputs_read_completely': True,
+    'no_current_credit_before_matching_active_binding': True,
+}
+row['original_omission_reassessments'] = []  # 원 omissions가 없을 때만 빈 목록
+claim['inherited_legal_blockers'] = job['carried_legal_blockers'][uid][cid]  # 해당 claim만
+claim['original_legal_negatives'] = job['reconsidered_legal_negatives'][uid][cid]  # 수정된 negative만
+claim['body_negative_reassessment'] = {
+    'original_negatives_sha256': queue.digest(claim['original_legal_negatives']),
+    'changed_statement_sha256': job['body_correction_review']['changed_statement_sha256s'][cid],
+    'edit_span_sha256s': job['body_correction_review']['edit_span_sha256s'],
+    'original_negative_read_completely': True,
+    'corrected_statement_read_completely': True,
+    'finding': '원 negative와 실제 수정 내용 및 primary 근거를 비교한 독립 판단',
+    'decision': 'UNRESOLVED_REMAINS_HELD',
+}
+```
+
+원 omission이 있으면 `job['body_correction_review']['parent_omissions']`의 각 정확한
+raw SHA에 대해 `omission_sha256`, 실제 `finding`, decision을 하나씩 기록한다.
+Decision은 `RESOLVED_BY_FRESH_COMPLETE_BODY_CENSUS_REVIEW` 또는
+`UNRESOLVED_REMAINS_OMISSION`이다. 미해소 원 omission 문자열은 현재 `omissions`에도
+그대로 남겨야 한다. 새 누락도 별도로 열거하며 COMPLETE를 강제하지 않는다.
+
+수정 명제의 KEEP은 `RESOLVED_BY_CHANGED_BODY_AND_PROPOSITION` decision과 현재
+공식 primary authority가 있어야 한다. 모든 KEEP authority는 기존 exact section,
+HTTPS URL, 시행일/미확정 한계, evidence path/raw SHA와 함께 다음 실제 확보 이력을 넣는다.
+
+```json
+{
+  "source_retrieval": {
+    "mode": "LIVE",
+    "http_status": 200,
+    "transport": "실제 검증 TLS/proxy/도구 경로",
+    "document_identity_status": "OFFICIAL_DOCUMENT_TARGET_PROVISIONS_DIRECTLY_READ",
+    "raw_sha256": "authority.evidence_sha256와 같은 실제 확보 payload SHA",
+    "retrieved_at_utc": "실제 최초 확보 timestamp",
+    "read_at_utc": "실제 문서 확인 timestamp"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+같은 날의 진짜 보존 payload 재독이면 mode는 `SAME_DAY_RETAINED_CACHE`이고 최초
+retrieved timestamp를 유지한다. 새 live 요청으로 표시하지 않는다. Read date는
+`law_checked_date`와 같아야 하며 retrieval ≤ read ≤ reviewed 순서와 동일한 source day를
+검사한다. HTTP403/404/200 access page는 문서 확인이 아니다. 실제 근거를 못 확보하면
+SOURCE_BLOCKED/HOLD로 남긴다. 효력일을 retrieval date로 대신하지 않는다.
+이 계약은 controller-attested reading/provenance와 커밋 바이트 결박을 검증하며,
+문서를 실제로 읽었다는 인간/actor의 주장을 암호학적으로 증명하지는 않는다.
+
+## Builder·shallow reader와 공개 blocker
+
+공개 metadata reader는 HEAD에 보존한 raw snapshot/report/envelope/source만 검증한다.
+옛 worker Git object는 필요 없다. Root의 submit/integrate는 기존 worker branch·정확 HEAD·
+allowed path·token 검사를 계속 요구한다. 원 census-only 이력은 명시적으로 보존된 old
+body snapshot으로만 검증하며, 일반 census-only body 금지 검사를 완화하지 않는다.
+
+`registered_specs`는 독립 결과가 통합되고 실제 effective body가 정확히 후보와 일치할
+때에만 새 census를 builder에 제공한다. 후보 revision을 `load_notes`로 활성화하지 않는다.
+잘못된 spec, 미통합 활성 body, raw source 변조는 실패한다. Census/body successors는
+원장 순서대로 explicit supersedence를 적용한다. 마지막 선택 census의 body SHA는
+실제 effective body와 같아야 한다.
+
+**공개 body migration은 구현하지 않았다.** 모든 후보와 job contract의 blocker는
+`ROOT_SEPARATE_16_FROM_ACTUALLY_PUBLISHED_15_SNAPSHOT`이다. 아직 공개되지 않은
+15번째 annotation guard로 body 교정을 통과시키지 않는다. Root는 실제 15번째 출시
+snapshot을 확보한 후 별도 16번째 decoder/manifest 및 공개·derived 재검증을 해야 한다.
+Full published builder 실행도 현재 후보에는 `NOT_RUN_INACTIVE_BODY_PUBLICATION_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_16`이다.
+
+## 최초 실제 후보 w3-a-3
+
+`revisions/notes/candidates/2026-11-04-w3-a-3-pamphlet-scope-v1.json`과
+`reports/full-corpus-review/body-corrections/w3-a-3-v1/record.json`이 R 저자 후보다.
+원 C fifth-c의 85 claims/보고서·원 target23 claims·omissions[]·HOLD011/019를 보존했다.
+§21의 pamphlet trigger가 opioid/narcotic만인 것처럼 좁혀진 마지막 단락만 교정했다.
+새 census24 claims에서 원22 statements는 그대로이며019를 고치고024를 분리했다.
+원011은 mandatory HOLD, 수정019/024는 fresh independent 재판단 전 SOURCE_BLOCKED다.
+
+2026-11-04 검증 TLS로 실제 확보·직접 읽은 Massachusetts 공식 §21과 Act2025c16
+§§7/27의 payload와 raw SHA를 evidence에 보존했다. Act §7의 보호 의료 제공자 요청 시
+label-name 예외는 §27에 따라2026-01-01 시행이며 pamphlet trigger amendment로
+취급하지 않는다. Consolidated §21의 첫 label paragraph와 해당 session-law 반영 차이,
+나이 용어 승계와 general IV narcotic 문법 해석, pamphlet 개별 시행일 한계는 남긴다.
+다른 단락의 새 전체 source review date나 독립 PASS를 만들지 않았다. R는 이 새
+body/census의 저자이므로 이 후보를 독립 reviewer로 claim할 수 없다.
+
+검증:
+
+```sh
+python -m pytest -q tests/test_notes_body_reassessment.py tests/test_note_review_queue.py \
+  tests/test_notes_census_reassessment.py tests/test_notes_independent_metadata.py
+```
+
+테스트의 작은 Git repo, authority·HTTP/source payload 및 미래16 activation은 명시적
+synthetic fixture다. 실제 원장 등록·법규 감사·출시 증거로 사용하지 않는다.

+# Native current-ID author review: exactly three SATA candidates
+
+The next order is **actual G author review → actual F/C independent review → root
+QA/publication**. The unchanged question objects MA-RW-0081/0082/0083 receive no
+credit from metadata conversion, the earlier G drafts or E's earlier draft audit.
+The source objects and their whole-record hashes do not change in this step.
+
+The derived ledger initially has `current_id_author_review_required: true`,
+`checked_at: null`, `author_review_increment: 0`. The original G draft date is kept
+separately in `source_author_review_date`. Author planning can select this explicit
+three-ID gap, and independent planning excludes it until formal author review is
+consumed. The original FIRST cohort and original 52 integrated jobs remain intact.
+The old static source list actually has **63 files**, all pinned without changes.
+
+Root controller sequence (workers must not write queue/ledger/registry):
+
+```sh
+# Regenerate the authoritative inventory with the new code first.
+python scripts/review_queue.py --stage author plan --size 3
+python scripts/review_queue.py --stage author claim --worker /root/independent_case_g
+```
+
+The sole required actor is the actual content author G. E is the engineer; E does
+not perform this legal review. The generated job records its three IDs and exact
+current whole-record hashes, `required_author_actor_id`, and
+`selection_policy: CURRENT_ID_AUTHOR_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. G is allowed at the author
+stage; G and E remain excluded from the later independent job.
+
+G reads the current compiled stem, every option/key and every Korean explanation,
+and verifies each tested proposition against current official primary text. If a
+wording/legal defect appears, report HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED; do not edit the question,
+key, G draft, existing source objects or metadata to manufacture agreement.
+
+G commits one report at
+`reports/full-corpus-review/sata-remediation-current-id-author/g-review.json`
+plus any new retained evidence under that directory's `evidence/` prefix. Existing
+retained public G source bytes may be referenced with their actual original
+retrieval dates. The report contract is:
+
+- `schema_version: sata-remediation-current-id-author-review/1`, `stage: author`,
+  exact `job_id`; `actor_provenance` has G's actual `actor_id`, `session_id` and
+  `stable_instance`, matching the original G provenance in each candidate.
+- `canonical_audit: false`, `canonical_release_credit: 0`,
+  `independent_of_authors: false`, `independent_review_credit: 0`.
+- Exactly three `records`, each with `question_id`, assigned `record_sha256`,
+  actual `checked_at`, `disposition` (KEEP/HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED/NEEDS_REMEDIATION),
+  `legal_review_status` (AUTHOR_SOURCE_CHECKED_NOT_INDEPENDENT, or
+  AUTHOR_CURRENT_ID_SOURCE_BLOCKED), `blocker`, and
+  `current_ID_stem_all_choices_key_all_Korean_explanations_read: true`.
+- Each record's `reviewer_provenance` repeats the actual G actor/session/stable
+  instance and `independent: false`; `author_expected_choice_ids` records the
+  author's expected set. KEEP must agree with the stored key. Unknown source
+  truth is `null`, with a null expected set and HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED.
+- `choice_by_choice_findings` contains every actual choice ID, with exact
+  `original_choice_text`, distinct Korean `finding_ko`, `exact_authority`,
+  boolean `expected_true` (null only for an unresolved held option), and a
+  nonempty `authorities` list.
+- Each authority has official HTTPS `official_url`, `exact_section`, actual
+  `law_checked_date`, explicit `version_or_effective_date_status`,
+  `body_verified_current_primary`, `http_status`, `used_as_legal_proof`, retained
+  repository `raw_path`/`raw_sha256`, and retained JSON
+  `retrieval_metadata_path`/`retrieval_metadata_sha256`. Metadata's `official_url`,
+  `http_status`, and `raw_sha256` must agree. HTTP failure or a wrong 200 body
+  cannot support KEEP; held failure evidence must set `used_as_legal_proof:false`,
+  a `failure_reason`, and an actual blocker. Unknown effective dates remain unknown.
+
+The record must also pass existing `build_full_corpus_review.validate_review`.
+This contract validates provenance/bindings; it is not automatic legal truth or
+identity authentication. Root must dispatch the job to the actual G session.
+
+After G commits, G returns an **uncommitted post-commit result envelope** with
+`stage: author`, exact `job_id`, `question_hashes`, `worker_commit`, the same actual
+`actor_provenance`, and the four zero/false credit declarations above. `results`
+contains exactly the three IDs, common `evidence_path` and report raw
+`evidence_sha256`, and a native disposition: AUTHOR_REVIEWED for a KEEP record,
+otherwise the matching HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED/NEEDS_REMEDIATION. No self-referential
+worker SHA is added to the committed report.
+
+Root cherry-picks the evidence, uses the normal author `submit` and sequential
+`integrate` commands, then commits the integrated queue and this explicit registry:
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema_version": "sata-remediation-native-author-sources/1",
+  "sources": [{
+    "job_id": "<actual native author job53 ID>",
+    "report_path": "reports/full-corpus-review/sata-remediation-current-id-author/g-review.json",
+    "report_sha256": "<actual committed report raw SHA-256>"
+  }]
+}
+```
+
+Registry path:
+`reports/full-corpus-review/sata-remediation-current-id-author-sources.json`.
+Only this one explicit three-ID source is accepted. Until registry, report, source
+bytes and integrated queue all match committed HEAD, the consumer gives no credit
+or fails closed. It checks current hashes, required actor, lease binding and the

+review source bytes are immutable. Runtime reads retained HEAD bytes and never
+fetches or resolves historical worker commits; native integration retains its
+existing fresh worker-commit check.
+
+Regenerate the inventory only after that commit. The actual three author records

+native review. No independent/canonical credit is created, including for held
+source failures. Root can then plan `independent-legacy --size 3` with the existing
+`--prioritize-remediation-and-default` option for another actual F/C session.

+# 기본 연습 문항의 실제 별도 세션 검토 — wave9
+
+Root가 현재 authoritative ledger와 publication/selection SHA에 따라 독립 미검토
+기본 문항 160개를 40개씩 배정했다. 연속 번호를 가정하지 않는다. 네 job의
+sequence는 30–33이며 `independent-legacy-work-queue.json`에 고정되어 있다.
+각 worker는 자신의 assignment와 visible packet만으로 시작하는 실제 새 세션이다.
+이 문서는 법적 정답이나 이전 검토자 판정을 제공하지 않는다.
+
+먼저 `docs/RELEASE_POLICY.md`, `docs/AUDIT_WORKFLOW.md`,
+`docs/SOURCE_USE_POLICY.md`, `docs/QUESTION_AUTHORING_STANDARD.md`, 현재
+`reports/full-corpus-review/progress.json`과 자신의 assignment를 읽는다.
+보고·검토 근거는 한국어, 원문 문항은 영어다. 원문·키·기존 해설·hash·history를
+worker가 수정하지 않는다. 다른 reviewer의 보고서나 author의 숨은 truth 배열을
+법적 근거 또는 독립 판단 대신 읽지 않는다.
+
+각자의 입력은 `reports/full-corpus-review/phase9-LETTER-evidence/assigned-visible-input.json`이다.
+Root가 정확한 current whole-record hash와 원래 stem·모든 choices·저장 key·전체
+한국어 explanation을 추출했다. 법규 근거가 아니라 검토할 원문이다. 필요한 원
+source/notes 링크는 해당 원 bank에서 찾되 hidden author judgement를 가져오지 않는다.
+
+모든 stem과 모든 option을 읽고, 각 proposition을 current Massachusetts/federal
+공식 primary 원문과 대조한다. 수치·기한·주체·면허·예외·의무/권고·연방/주 차이를
+구별한다. CORRECT/INCORRECT 극성과 SATA의 정확한 조합을 별도로 계산한다.
+한국어 core와 모든 distractor rationale 및 learning boundary도 읽는다.
+공식 URL, exact section, 적용 시행일/버전 또는 실제 미확정 한계, 실제 review date와
+timezone-aware retrieval/read timestamp, 실제 HTTP 상태·문서 정체·raw SHA를 기록한다.
+
+정상 검증 TLS를 쓰는 urllib 등으로 공식 자료를 확보할 수 있다. 검색 도구 실패를
+법적 근거로 쓰지 않는다. HTTP403/404나 200 access/error page는 원문 확인이 아니다.
+확보한 공식 정부 문서의 원 payload·추출문·retrieval metadata를 자기 evidence 경로에
+보존한다. 같은 날 실제 official retained bytes를 재독했다면 원 retrieval timestamp와
+cache 재독임을 밝힌다. 미확인·모순·중요 시행일 미확정은 HOLD/SOURCE_BLOCKED와
+정확한 blocker로 남긴다. citation·effective date·read assertion을 만들어내지 않는다.
+
+현재 style profile/blueprint를 읽고 현실성도 별도로 판단한다. 공개 허가된 NABP
+sample/blueprint 안내로 공개 형식만 확인하며 보호된 exam/recalled/Pre-MPJE/commercial
+item을 복사하지 않는다. 저작권 raw는 repo에 새로 공개하지 않고 실제 확인 URL·SHA·
+최소 scope와 자체 작성한 memo만 보존한다. 각 문항의 실제 상황, 역할/행동/법적
+결정, distractor plausibility, answer cue/복제/내용 없는 문구를 직접 평가한다.
+유사도 도구는 후보 찾기 용도이며 최종 판정을 대신하지 않는다. 가까운 stem과
+전 choices를 직접 읽어 중복/맥락을 평가한다. 새로운 학습범위를 허위로 주장하지 않는다.
+
+자기 실제 세션이 이전에 해당 원문의 whole-key 결론을 평가했거나 author/editor였다면
+그 이력을 기록하고 새 독립 key 판단으로 세지 않는다. 새 identity 문자열로 우회하지 않는다.
+Source가 검증돼도 결함이 있으면 KEEP을 강제하지 않는다. 잘못된 키, 모호한 범위,
+해설 오류, 현실성 문제를 구별하고 구체적인 후속 조치와 필요한 새 상황을 제안한다.

+`auditor_instance`, `independent_of_authors: true`, `canonical_audit: false`,
+`canonical_release_credit: 0`, `author_review_credit: 0`, 실제 review date를 가진다.
+정확히 배정된 40 records 각각은 question_id/current record_sha256, 원문 실독 scope,
+legal_review(existing_answer_correct, verdict, stored/expected keys, polarity,
+모든 option별 원문·truth/support·한국어 finding·exact primary authorities,

+AN ACT STRENGTHENING HEALTH CARE PROTECTIONS IN THE COMMONWEALTH
+Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General Court assembled, and by the authority of the same, as follows:
+SECTION 1. Clause Twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4 of the General Laws, as amended by section 1 of chapter 363 of the acts of 2024, is hereby further amended by adding the following subclause:-
+(x) the name, home address, personal email address, home telephone number or mobile telephone number and any other personal information of an individual engaged in the provision, facilitation or promotion of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12.
+SECTION 2. Section 11I1/2 of chapter 12 of the General Laws, as appearing in the 2022 Official Edition, is hereby amended by adding the following 3 subsections:-
+(g) Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary and except as required by federal law, no state or local agency of the commonwealth or officer or employee or any other person acting on behalf of a state or local agency of the commonwealth while acting under the color of law shall cooperate with or provide information or assistance to any federal law enforcement agency or other agency or any other state or local law enforcement agency or other agency or any individual or quasi-law enforcement agent or expend or use any time, money, facilities, property, equipment, personnel or other resources in relation to an investigation or inquiry into services constituting legally-protected health care activity if such services would be lawful as provided had they occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
+(h) Evidence relating to the involvement of an individual in any legally-protected health care activity shall not be offered as evidence that such individual has engaged in wrongdoing, whether civil, criminal, professional or otherwise, by virtue of the fact that the individual who received such services was not physically present in the commonwealth when they received such services. Nothing in this section shall prevent a party from offering such evidence in a proceeding that: (i) sounds in tort or contract; (ii) is actionable, in an equivalent or similar manner, under the laws of the commonwealth; and (iii) was brought by the patient who received reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services or the patient’s legal representative.
+(i) The attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive or other equitable relief to enforce this section.
+SECTION 3. Section 12 of chapter 12C of the General Laws is hereby amended by striking out subsection (b), as so appearing, and inserting in place thereof the following 8 subsections:-
+(b) The center shall permit a government agency or authority to access identifiable health information of an individual only to the extent necessary for such government agency or authority to accomplish the public purposes for which access was given, subject to subsection (f). Except as required by federal law, the center shall not provide access to any data, including de-identified data or any other data that would allow the identification of a patient or provider in response to an out-of-state or federal inquiry or investigation into services constituting legally-protected health care activity, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12.
+(c) The center shall permit providers, provider organizations and public and private health care payers access to identifiable health information of an individual solely for the purposes of carrying out treatment, payment or health care operations.
+(d) The center may disclose identifiable health information of an individual for research, regardless of the source of funding of the research; provided, however, that: (i) the center obtains documentation of authorization from the individual patient; or (ii) waiver of individual authorization has been approved by either an institutional review board or privacy board.
+(e) The center may disclose de-identified health information of an individual for the purposes of lowering total medical expenses, coordinating care, benchmarking, quality analysis, research, administrative or planning purposes, informing consumer health care decisions or other purposes that aim to improve healthcare or public health outcomes for commonwealth residents that are consistent with the goals of this chapter. A recipient of de-identified health information of an individual shall not use such information or data to identify any person for any purpose.
+(f) A recipient of de-identified or identifiable health information of an individual patient shall not use such information to: (i) conduct a criminal, civil or administrative investigation into any individual patient; or (ii) impose criminal, civil or administrative liability on any individual patient.
+(g) Access to identifiable health information of an individual, including personal data as defined in section 1 of chapter 66A, authorized under this section shall be deemed to comply with the requirements of chapter 66A.
+(h) The center may charge an application fee or other fees sufficient to process and provide such access to non-governmental entities.
+(i) A violation of subsection (f), or any rule or regulation issued thereunder, shall constitute a violation of chapter 93A.
+SECTION 4. Section 75 of chapter 31 of the General Laws, as appearing in section 161 of chapter 238 of the acts of 2024, is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph:-
+Nothing in this section shall be construed to permit civil service employees to furnish information to, or cooperate with, law enforcement authorities in contravention of section 11I1/2 of chapter 12 or section 63 of chapter 147.
+SECTION 5. Section 10B of chapter 66 of the General Laws is hereby amended by striking out, in lines 34 and 35, as appearing in the 2022 Official Edition, the words “persons providing or training in family planning services” and inserting in place thereof the following words:- persons engaged or trained in the provision, facilitation or promotion of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12,.
+SECTION 6. Chapter 93 of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the following section:-
+Section 115. (a) As used in this section, the following words shall have the following meanings unless the context clearly requires otherwise:
+“Electronic communication”, any transfer of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data or intelligence of any nature transmitted in whole or in part by a wire, radio, electromagnetic, photoelectronic or photo-optical system; provided, however, that such term shall not include any communication: (i) made through a tone only paging device; or (ii) that is disseminated by the sender through a method of transmission that is configured so that such communication is readily accessible to the public.
+“Electronic communication services”, any service which provides to users thereof the ability to send or receive wire or electronic communications.
+“Remote computing service”, as defined in 18 U.S.C. 2711.
+(b) A business entity that operates in the commonwealth and provides electronic communication services or remote computing service to residents of the commonwealth or to a business entity organized under the laws of the commonwealth shall not comply with a subpoena, warrant or other civil or criminal legal process for records, information or assistance that the business entity knows relates to a resident, health care provider or business entity in the commonwealth in connection with legally-protected health care activity as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, except as required by a valid federal law, unless the subpoena, warrant or other civil or criminal legal process includes, or is accompanied by, an attestation, made under penalty of perjury, stating that the subpoena, warrant or other civil or criminal legal process does not seek documents, information or testimony relating to an investigation into, or the enforcement of, another state’s law that asserts criminal or civil liability for the provision, receipt, attempted provision or receipt, assistance in the provision or receipt or attempted assistance in the provision or receipt of legally-protected health care activity that is lawful in the commonwealth.
+(c) Any false attestation submitted under this section shall be subject to a statutory penalty of not more than $50,000 per violation. Submission of an attestation shall subject the attester to the jurisdiction of the courts of the commonwealth for any suit, penalty or damages arising out of a false attestation under this section.
+(d) The attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive or other equitable relief to compel any business entity that operates in the commonwealth and that provides electronic communications services or remote computing service to residents of the commonwealth or to a business entity organized under the laws of the commonwealth to comply with this section.
+SECTION 7. Section 21 of chapter 94C of the General Laws is hereby amended by striking out the first paragraph, as appearing in the 2022 Official Edition, and inserting in place thereof the following 2 paragraphs:-
+The pharmacist filling a written, electronic or oral prescription for a controlled substance shall package the controlled substance in a container, affixing to the container a label showing the date of filling, the pharmacy name and address, the filling pharmacist's initials, the serial number of the prescription, the name of the patient, unless it is a veterinary prescription, the name of the prescribing practitioner except as otherwise provided in this section, the name of the controlled substance, directions for use and cautionary statements, if any, contained in such prescription or required by law, and if the controlled substance is dispensed as tablets or capsules, the number of same in such container.
+Except as required by federal law, the label for a controlled substance prescribed for reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, shall, at the request of the provider, include the name of the prescribing health care practice instead of the name of the prescribing practitioner; provided, however, that a pharmacy benefit manager, as defined in section 1 of chapter 176Y, shall not recoup or recover funds from a pharmacy due to the absence of such dispensing practitioner’s name under this paragraph. The department may promulgate regulations to implement this paragraph.
+SECTION 8. Section 22 of said chapter 94C, as so appearing, is hereby amended by adding the following subsection:-
+(d) Notwithstanding subsection (b) and to the extent allowable under federal law, the label for a controlled substance prescribed for reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, may include the name and address of the dispensing health care practice instead of the name and address of the dispensing practitioner.
+SECTION 9. Paragraph (1) of subsection (a) of section 24A of said chapter 94C, as so appearing, is hereby amended by adding the following sentence:- Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, medications that may be prescribed for reproductive health care services and gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, shall be excluded from the prescription monitoring program unless reporting of such is determined by the department to be necessary to protect the public health.
+SECTION 10. Said section 24A of said chapter 94C, as so appearing, is hereby further amended by adding the following subsection:-
+(n) Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, except as required by federal law, the department shall not provide disaggregated data or individually identifiable data from the prescription drug monitoring program to a federal law enforcement agency or other agency or any other state or local law enforcement agency or other agency or any private citizen or entity or quasi-law enforcement agent in relation to an investigation or inquiry into reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, if such services would be lawful as provided had they occurred entirely in the commonwealth. This section shall not be construed to apply to prescription drugs for usages, including off-label usages, that are unrelated to reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services.
+SECTION 11. Chapter 111 of the General Laws is hereby amended by inserting after section 51 the following section:-
+Section 511/4. (a) For purposes of this section, the following words shall have the following meanings unless the context clearly requires otherwise:
+“Emergency medical condition”, a medical condition manifesting itself by acute symptoms of sufficient severity such that the absence of immediate medical attention could reasonably be expected to result in: (i) placing the health of the patient in serious jeopardy; (ii) serious impairment of bodily functions; or (iii) serious dysfunction of any bodily organ or part; provided, however, that “emergency medical condition” shall include, but shall not be limited to, ectopic pregnancy, complications of pregnancy loss or abortion, active labor, risks to future fertility, preterm premature rupture of membranes, placental abruption or bleeding from placenta previa or emergent hypertensive disorders, such as preeclampsia and eclampsia and peripartum cardiomyopathy, and any other condition a licensed health care provider, acting within their lawful scope of practice, determines, in the provider’s best medical judgment, to be an emergency medical condition.
+“Patient”, any person who presents at a hospital or who is brought to a hospital by ambulance or specialized emergency medical services vehicle as defined in section 1 of chapter 111C.
+“Stabilizing treatment”, includes abortion when abortion is necessary to resolve the patient’s injury or emergency medical condition.
+(b) Acute-care hospitals licensed under section 51G, during all operating hours of an emergency department or a satellite emergency facility as defined in section 511/2, shall provide hospital emergency services to any patient who presents with an injury or an emergency medical condition. Acute-care hospitals shall furnish hospital emergency services, including, but not limited to, medical screening by qualified medical personnel, to reach with reasonable clinical confidence a determination of whether a patient has an emergency medical condition and to provide necessary stabilizing treatment for patients with an emergency medical condition. Acute-care hospitals shall establish and maintain policies and procedures for the provision of hospital emergency services, including for a patient’s refusal to consent, restricting transfers until the patient is stabilized, appropriate transfers of patients, nondiscrimination in providing services to patients, preventing delay in examination or treatment of patients and whistleblower protections.          (c) The department may promulgate regulations to implement this section.
+(d) The attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive or other equitable relief to enforce this section. In any action brought by the attorney general under this section, the court may also award a civil penalty of not more than $10,000 for each violation.
+SECTION 12. Said chapter 111 is hereby further amended by inserting after section 70H the following section:-
+Section 70I. (a) For the purposes of this section, the following words shall have the following meanings unless the context clearly requires otherwise:
+“Abortion”, as defined in section 12K of chapter 112.
+“Abortion-related health care services”, all supplies, care and services of a medical, behavioral health, mental health, surgical, psychiatric, therapeutic, diagnostic, preventative, rehabilitative or supportive nature relating to miscarriage management or the termination of a pregnancy.
+“Business”, (i) a business organized for the purpose of maintaining medical information to make an individual’s medical information available to the individual or to a health care provider at the request of the individual or a health care provider, for purposes of allowing the individual or the provider to manage the individual’s medical information or for the diagnosis and treatment of the individual;
+(ii) a business that offers medical recordkeeping, electronic health records or electronic medical record services, including, but not limited to, software or hardware, to consumers that makes an individual’s medical information available to another person or a health care provider at the request of the individual or a health care provider, for purposes of allowing the other person or the provider to manage the individual’s medical information or for the diagnosis, treatment or management of a medical condition of the individual;
+(iii) a business that is licensed by the department or the department of mental health to provide medical, clinical, behavioral or health services; or          (iv) a business that offers a digital service to a consumer for the purpose of allowing such consumer to manage the consumer’s reproductive or sexual health information or for the diagnosis, treatment or management of a reproductive or sexual health medical condition of the consumer.
+“Gender-affirming health care services”, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12.
+(b) A business that electronically stores or maintains medical information related to the provision of abortion or abortion-related health care services, in vitro fertilization and gender-affirming health care services, including, but not limited to, on an electronic health record system or electronic medical record system, on behalf of a health care provider, health care insurance plan, pharmaceutical company, pharmacy benefit manager, contractor or employer, shall develop capabilities, policies and procedures to enable and shall enable features that:
+(i) limit user access privileges to information systems that contain medical information related to abortion or abortion-related health care services, in vitro fertilization and gender-affirming health care services only to those persons who are authorized in writing by the patient to access such medical information;
+(ii) prevent the disclosure, access, transfer, transmission or processing of medical information related to abortion or abortion-related health care services, in vitro fertilization or gender-affirming health care services to persons and entities outside of the commonwealth, absent the express written consent of the patient, independent of any other agreement, that specifically authorizes the disclosure, access, transfer, transmission or processing of such medical information to the named persons or entities outside of the commonwealth; and
+(iii) automatically disable access by individuals and entities outside the commonwealth to segregated medical information related to abortion or abortion-related health care services, in vitro fertilization or gender-affirming health care services, absent the express written consent of the patient that specifically authorizes access by named persons or entities outside of the commonwealth to such segregated medical information.
+(c) The department may promulgate such regulations as may be necessary to implement this section.
+(d) The department shall create a consent form that meets the requirements of this section and shall require its use by all licensed health care providers in the commonwealth.
+(e) The attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive or other equitable relief to enforce this section. In any action brought by the attorney general under this section, the court may also award a civil penalty of not more than $5,000 per violation.
+(f) A business that discloses, transfers or processes information solely for the purposes of payment, treatment or health care operations, as defined by 45 CFR 164.501, shall not be in violation of this section.
+SECTION 13. Section 12Q of chapter 112 of the General Laws, as appearing in the 2022 Official Edition, is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph:-
+The commissioner of public health shall not collect, maintain, use, disclose or disseminate disaggregated surveillance data or individually identifiable surveillance data on abortions performed in the commonwealth. The name, home address, personal email address, home telephone number and mobile telephone number of individuals engaged in the provision, facilitation or promotion of reproductive health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, shall not be considered a public record under chapter 66.
+SECTION 14. Said chapter 112 is hereby further amended by inserting after section 12Q the following section:- Section 12Q1/2. The commissioner of public health shall not collect, maintain or use individually identifiable data on gender-affirming health care services provided in the commonwealth, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, except as authorized by law, and shall not disclose or disseminate disaggregated data or individually identifiable surveillance data on gender-affirming health care services provided in the commonwealth. The name, home address, personal email address, home telephone number and mobile telephone number of individuals engaged in the provision, facilitation or promotion of gender-affirming health care services shall not be considered a public record under chapter 66.
+SECTION 15. Section 61 of said chapter 112, as most recently amended by section 2 of chapter 353 of the acts of 2024, is hereby further amended by adding the following 3 paragraphs:-
+Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, no person shall be subject to discipline by a board of registration, including through the revocation, suspension or cancellation of a certificate, registration or license, or a reprimand, censure or monetary fine, for providing or assisting in the provision of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as those terms are defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or for any judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from the health care services if the services as provided would have been lawful and consistent with the standard of conduct for the designated profession had they occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
+No board of registration shall make available for public dissemination on an individual’s profile the record of any criminal conviction or charge for a felony or serious misdemeanor, final disciplinary action by a licensing board in another state or a malpractice court judgment, arbitration award or settlement that resulted from providing or assisting in the provision of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services or for any judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from the health care services if the services as provided would have been lawful and consistent with the scope and standards of practice for the designated profession had they occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
+No board of registration shall take adverse action on an application for a certificate, registration or licensure based on a criminal or civil action or disciplinary action by a licensing board of another state or a medical malpractice claim in another state that resulted from providing or assisting in the provision of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services that, as provided, would have been lawful and consistent with the standard of conduct for the designated profession had the health care services occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
+SECTION 16. Section 26 of chapter 119 of the General Laws, as appearing in the 2022 Official Edition, is hereby amended by adding the following subsection:-
+(d) The removal of a child from the care or custody of a parent, custodian or guardian in another jurisdiction based on the parent, custodian or guardian allowing their child to seek or receive gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, shall not provide a basis for adjudicating the child in need of care and protection under this section unless the conduct of the parent, custodian or guardian would otherwise constitute abuse or neglect under the laws of the commonwealth.
+SECTION 17. Section 63 of chapter 147 of the General Laws, as so appearing, is hereby amended by striking out subsection (b) and inserting in place thereof the following 2 subsections:-
+(b) Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary and except as required by federal law, no state or local law enforcement agency or officer or employee or any other person acting on behalf of a state or local law enforcement agency of the commonwealth, while acting under color of law, shall provide information or assistance to a federal law enforcement agency or any other state’s agency, including a law enforcement agency, or any private citizen or quasi-law enforcement agent, or expend or use time, money, facilities, property, equipment, personnel or other resources in relation to an investigation or inquiry into services constituting legally-protected health care activity, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, if the services would be lawful as provided had the services occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
+(c) The attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive or other equitable relief to enforce this section.
+SECTION 18. Chapter 175 of the General Laws is hereby amended by inserting after section 193U the following section:-
+Section 193V. No insurance company offering for sale any policy of insurance shall discriminate against an organization that is exempt from taxation under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or adjust or otherwise calculate such organization’s risk classification or premium charges in the provision of any form of liability insurance covering negligence, wrongful acts, errors or omissions of the organization and its respective members, directors and officers, on the basis that: (i) the organization offers reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as those terms are defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12; (ii) the organization engages in legally-protected health care activity, as defined in said section 11I1/2 of said chapter 12; or (iii) the organization is or has been the subject of abusive litigation, as defined in said section 11I1/2 of said chapter 12. Nothing herein shall prohibit such insurers from establishing reasonable classifications of risks and premium charges based upon the relative risk associated with practice in a particular specialty.
+SECTION 19. Chapter 176Q of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the following section:-
+Section 19. (a) Except as required by federal law, the connector shall not provide access to any data, including de-identified data or any other data that would allow the identification of a patient, applicant or provider, in response to an out-of-state or federal inquiry or investigation into services constituting legally-protected health care activity, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12.
+(b) The connector shall grant providers, provider organizations and public and private health care payers access to identifiable health information or other personally identifiable information of an individual solely for the purposes of carrying out treatment, payment, health care operations or its functions as a health insurance exchange.
+(c) The connector shall not disclose, disseminate, transfer or otherwise allow access to identifiable health information or other personally identifiable information of an individual for any purpose not expressly authorized by this chapter.
+(d) A recipient of de-identified or identifiable health information or other personally identifiable information of an individual patient or applicant shall not use such information to: (i) conduct a criminal, civil or administrative investigation into any individual patient; or (ii) impose criminal, civil or administrative liability on any individual patient.
+SECTION 20. Chapter 208 of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the following section:-
+Section 56. (a) A law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services shall not provide a basis to alter custody, parenting time or visitation or be used to make a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment in a case pending in a court in the commonwealth, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian under such law would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(b) No court in the commonwealth shall admit or consider a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment based on a parent or guardian allowing their child to receive or seek gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or a finding that a parent or guardian is criminally, civilly or otherwise liable for violating another state’s law that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services as evidence in any proceeding with respect to that parent or guardian and any of their children, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(c) Notwithstanding any provision of this chapter to the contrary, when deciding whether to alter custody, parenting time or visitation, a court in the commonwealth shall consider the likely disruption or cessation of gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, as a result of a law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that prohibits gender-affirming health care services or authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming care health care services.
+SECTION 21. Chapter 209A of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the following section:-
+Section 12. (a) Notwithstanding section 5A or any other general or special law to the contrary, a law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services shall not provide a basis to alter custody, parenting time or visitation or be used to make a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment in a case pending in a court in the commonwealth, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(b) Notwithstanding section 5A or any other general or special law to the contrary, no court in the commonwealth shall admit or consider a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment based on a parent or guardian allowing their child to receive or seek gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or a finding that a parent or guardian is criminally, civilly or otherwise liable for violating another state’s law that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services as evidence in any proceeding in which such parent or guardian and any of such parent’s or guardian’s children are parties, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(c) Notwithstanding section 5A or any other general or special law to the contrary, when deciding whether to alter custody, parenting time or visitation, a court in the commonwealth shall consider the likely disruption or cessation of gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, as a result of a law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that prohibits gender-affirming health care services or authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming care health care services.
+SECTION 22. Chapter 209B of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the following section:-
+Section 15. (a) A law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming care health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services shall not provide a basis to alter custody, parenting time or visitation or be used to make a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment in a case pending in a court in the commonwealth, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(b) No court in the commonwealth shall admit or consider a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment based on a parent or guardian allowing their child to receive or seek gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or a finding that a parent or guardian is criminally, civilly or otherwise liable for violating another state’s law that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services as evidence in any proceeding with respect to that parent or guardian and any of their children, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(c) Notwithstanding any provision of this chapter to the contrary, when deciding whether to alter custody, parenting time or visitation, a court in the commonwealth shall consider the likely disruption or cessation of gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, as a result of a law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that prohibits gender-affirming health care services or authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming care health care services.
+SECTION 23. Chapter 209C of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the following section:-
+Section 28Q. (a) A law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services shall not provide a basis to alter custody, parenting time or visitation or be used to make a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment in a case pending in a court in the commonwealth, unless the conduct of the parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(b) No court in the commonwealth shall admit or consider a finding of abuse, neglect or maltreatment based on a parent or guardian allowing their child to receive or seek gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, or a finding that a parent or guardian is criminally, civilly or otherwise liable for violating another state’s law that bans the provision of gender-affirming health care services as evidence in any proceeding in which such parent or guardian and any of such parent’s or guardian’s children are parties, unless the conduct of such parent or guardian would constitute abuse, neglect or maltreatment under the laws of the commonwealth.
+(c) Notwithstanding any provision of this chapter to the contrary, when deciding whether to alter custody, parenting time or visitation, a court in the commonwealth shall consider the likely disruption or cessation of gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, as a result of a law of a jurisdiction outside the commonwealth that prohibits gender-affirming health care services or authorizes a child to be removed from the care or custody of a parent or guardian based on the parent or guardian allowing their child to receive gender-affirming care health care services.
+SECTION 24. Chapter 221 of the General Laws is hereby amended by inserting after section 42 the following section:-
+Section 42A. Notwithstanding any general or special law or rule or regulation to the contrary, no attorney licensed in the commonwealth shall be removed or otherwise subject to discipline, including through the revocation, suspension or cancellation of the attorney’s license or reprimand, censure or monetary fine, for advising or representing a client or prospective client on or in a matter related to the provision of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as those terms are defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12, if the sole basis for such removal or discipline is that: (i) the client offered, provided or received reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services that are unlawful in another state; (ii) another state’s laws create actual or potential liability for the reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services offered, provided or received by the client; or (iii) the attorney is subject to actual or potential liability, or removal or discipline, in another jurisdiction based on the reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services offered, provided or received by the client; provided, however, that the attorney’s conduct shall otherwise comply with the laws of the commonwealth and meet the standards set forth in the rules of professional conduct promulgated by the supreme judicial court.
+SECTION 25. (a) The commissioner of public health shall convene a technical advisory group to review section 70I of chapter 111 of the General Laws to advise on technical aspects of the implementation of said section 70I of said chapter 111, including regulations necessary for implementation. Not later than July 1, 2026, the technical advisory group shall make recommendations to the house and senate committees on ways and means and the joint committee on the judiciary on measures necessary to mitigate restrictions on appropriate data sharing that limit interoperability to ensure access to necessary clinical information to maximize appropriate clinical care.
+(b) The technical advisory group shall explore and make recommendations on: (i) the standardization of service definitions and terminology and structured standardized data; (ii) reducing the administrative burden and impacts on clinical care of patient consent forms, including through the use of consent management platforms; (iii) mitigating restrictions of appropriate data sharing and limitations on interoperability that impact patient care; (iv) the appropriateness of exempting information accessed, used and disclosed for treatment, payment and health care operation purposes; and (v) minimizing penalties for a business that makes a good faith effort to implement said section 70I of said chapter 111.
+(c) The technical advisory group shall consist of the following members: the commissioner of public health or a designee, who shall serve as chair; a representative of the Massachusetts Health and Hospital Association, Inc.; a representative of the Massachusetts Medical Society; a representative of the Conference of Boston Teaching Hospitals, Inc.; a representative of the Planned Parenthood League of Massachusetts, Inc.; a representative of Fenway Health; a representative of the Massachusetts Association of Health Plans, Inc.; a representative of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Massachusetts, Inc.; a representative of the Massachusetts eHealth Institute; a representative of Health Care for All, Inc.; and 4 members to be appointed by the commissioner of public health, 1 of whom shall be a person with expertise in health information privacy, 1 of whom shall be a person with expertise in health information technology and 2 of whom shall be persons with lived experience accessing abortion-related health care services or gender-affirming health care services.

Section 21: Packaging and labeling by pharmacist filling prescription; distribution of educational pamphlet +

+

Section 21. The pharmacist filling a written, electronic or oral prescription for a controlled substance shall package the controlled substance in a container, affixing to the container a label showing the date of filling, the pharmacy name and address, the filling pharmacist's initials, the serial number of the prescription, the name of the patient, unless it is a veterinary prescription, the name of the prescribing practitioner, the name of the controlled substance, directions for use and cautionary statements, if any, contained in such prescription or required by law, and if the controlled substance is dispensed as tablets or capsules the number of same in such container.

+ +

Upon the request of an elderly person, as defined in section fourteen of chapter nineteen A or a person visually impaired, directions on the label affixed by the pharmacist to a container of a prescription drug shall be typed in a print size allowing no more than ten characters per inch.

+ +

The department, in consultation with relevant stakeholders and experts in the treatment and management of acute and chronic pain, and based in part on the Pain Management Best Practices Inter–Agency Task Force Report issued by the United States Department of Health and Human Services, shall produce and distribute, either in written or electronic form, to pharmacies, not including institutional pharmacies, pamphlets for consumers relative to narcotic drugs, including opiates, that shall include educational information related to: (i) pain management and the use and availability of non-opioid alternatives for the treatment of acute and chronic pain, including, but not limited to: (A) information on available non-opioid alternatives for the treatment of pain, including non-opioid medications and non-pharmacological therapies; and (B) the advantages and disadvantages of the use of such non-opioid treatment alternatives; (ii) the consumer's option to fill a prescription for a schedule II controlled substance in a lesser quantity than indicated on the prescription pursuant to subsection (d|b5) of section 18; (iii) misuse and abuse of narcotics by adults and children; (iv) the risk of dependency and addiction associated with narcotics use; (v) proper storage and disposal of narcotics; (vi) addiction support and treatment resources; (vii) the telephone helpline operated by the bureau of substance addiction services established in section 18 of chapter 17; (viii) the risks of unintended overdoses associated with prescription opioid use, including, but not limited to: (A) mixing any opioid with stimulants or respiratory depressants, including, but not limited to, alcohol and benzodiazepines; and (B) changes in personal tolerance levels for persons with a history of overdose; and (ix) risk reduction measures to prevent, respond to and reverse an opioid overdose. A pharmacist shall distribute the pamphlet when dispensing a narcotic or controlled substance contained in schedule II or III; provided, however, that pharmacists shall not be required to distribute the pamphlet if: (1) the patient is receiving outpatient palliative care pursuant to section 227 of chapter 111; (2) the patient is a resident of a long-term care facility; or (3) the narcotic or controlled substance is prescribed for use in the treatment of substance use disorder or opioid dependence. For the purposes of this section, non-opioid treatment alternatives shall include, but shall not be limited to, medications, restorative therapies, interventional procedures, behavioral health approaches and complementary and integrative treatments.

+ +

The labeling provisions of this section shall apply to the compounding and dispensing of drugs on the oral, electronic or written prescription of a licensed and registered prescriber under section 9. All drug preparations compounded, made or formulated by a pharmacy licensed by the board of registration in pharmacy shall have affixed to their container by the compounding pharmacy a label notifying prescribed users and practitioners that the drug is either a sterile or non-sterile compounded drug preparation.

+ +

All pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding and licensed under sections 39G to 39I, inclusive, of chapter 112 shall provide a telephone number to foster communication between patients in the commonwealth and a pharmacist employed by the pharmacy who has access to the patient's records. The phone shall be staffed during regular hours of operation every day and not less than 56 hours per week. The phone number shall be affixed to the drug's container, alongside the label notifying prescribed users and practitioners of the fact that the drug is a compounded drug preparation. This paragraph shall not apply to an institutional pharmacy licensed pursuant to section 39I of chapter 112 if the sterile drug preparation compounded by such pharmacy is to be administered to an individual admitted as an inpatient within the same hospital.

+    "title": "추가 label 요건과 특별 상황",
+    "body": "### Compounded preparation\n\nPharmacy가 compounded한 약에는 sterile 또는 nonsterile compounded drug preparation이라는 표시가 필요하다. Sterile 또는 complex nonsterile compounding pharmacy의 해당 label에는 pharmacy phone number와 법이 정한 staffed-hours 연락 정보 등이 추가된다. 동일 hospital의 inpatient에게 주는 경우의 예외를 일반 outpatient 처방에 확대하지 않는다. \n\nCompounding 표시, beyond-use date, manufacturer expiration date는 서로 다른 정보다. 제조사 제품을 단순히 다른 용기에 옮겼다는 사실만으로 모든 법적 분류가 동일해지지는 않는다. Compounding의 분류·허가·USP 상세는 Week 4에서 다룬다.\n\n### Large-print directions\n\n고령자 또는 visually impaired 환자의 해당 요청에는 directions를 inch당 10 characters를 넘지 않는 인쇄 크기로 표시하는 c.94C §21의 조건을 확인한다. 이것은 '10-point font'라는 규칙이 아니다. 글꼴 크기 단위와 characters-per-inch를 혼동하지 않는다. \n\n### Federal transfer warning\n\n해당 Schedule II·III·IV patient label에는 처방받은 환자 이외의 사람에게 약물을 넘기는 것이 연방법상 금지된다는 경고를 표시한다. 이 경고의 'transfer'는 환자 사이에서 약물을 주고받는 행위에 관한 것으로, pharmacist-to-pharmacist prescription-information transfer와 같은 의미가 아니다. Schedule VI 전체에 federal controlled-drug warning을 법적 필수사항이라고 일률적으로 붙이지 않는다. \n\n### Department 지정 환자 정보자료\n\nc.94C §21은 pharmacist의 지정 pamphlet 배포 trigger를 “a narcotic or controlled substance contained in schedule II or III”를 dispensing하는 경우로 규정한다. II·III controlled substance를 non-opioid라는 이유만으로 그 배포 대상에서 제외하지 않는다. Outpatient palliative care, LTCF resident, SUD treatment 등 조문의 예외를 함께 읽는다. Pharmacy가 임의로 만든 일반 leaflet이 모든 지정 자료의 요건을 자동 충족하는 것은 아니다.",

+AN ACT STRENGTHENING HEALTH CARE PROTECTIONS IN THE COMMONWEALTH
+Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General Court assembled, and by the authority of the same, as follows:
+SECTION 1. Clause Twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4 of the General Laws, as amended by section 1 of chapter 363 of the acts of 2024, is hereby further amended by adding the following subclause:-          (x) the name, home address, personal email address, home telephone number or mobile telephone number and any other personal information of an individual engaged in the provision, facilitation or promotion of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12.
+SECTION 2. Section 11I1/2 of chapter 12 of the General Laws, as appearing in the 2022 Official Edition, is hereby amended by adding the following 3 subsections:-          (g) Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary and except as required by federal law, no state or local agency of the commonwealth or officer or employee or any other person acting on behalf of a state or local agency of the commonwealth while acting under the color of law shall cooperate with or provide information or assistance to any federal law enforcement agency or other agency or any other state or local law enforcement agency or other agency or any individual or quasi-law enforcement agent or expend or use any time, money, facilities, property, equipment, personnel or other resources in relation to an investigation or inquiry into services constituting legally-protected health care activity if such services would be lawful as provided had they occurred entirely in the commonwealth.          (h) Evidence relating to the involvement of an individual in any legally-protected health care activity shall not be offered as evidence that such individual has engaged in wrongdoing, whether civil, criminal, professional or otherwise, by virtue of the fact that the individual who received such services was not physically present in the commonwealth when they received such services. Nothing in this section shall prevent a party from offering such evidence in a proceeding that: (i) sounds in tort or contract; (ii) is actionable, in an equivalent or similar manner, under the laws of the commonwealth; and (iii) was brought by the patient who received reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services or the patient’s legal representative.          (i) The attorney general may bring a civil action for injunctive or other equitable relief to enforce this section.
+SECTION 3. Section 12 of chapter 12C of the General Laws is hereby amended by striking out subsection (b), as so appearing, and inserting in place thereof the following 8 subsections:-          (b) The center shall permit a government agency or authority to access identifiable health information of an individual only to the extent necessary for such government agency or authority to accomplish the public purposes for which access was given, subject to subsection (f). Except as required by federal law, the center shall not provide access to any data, including de-identified data or any other data that would allow the identification of a patient or provider in response to an out-of-state or federal inquiry or investigation into services constituting legally-protected health care activity, as defined in section 11I1/2 of chapter 12.          (c) The center shall permit providers, provider organizations and public and private health care payers access to identifiable health information of an individual solely for the purposes of carrying out treatment, payment or health care operations.           (d) The center may disclose identifiable health information of an individual for research, regardless of the source of funding of the research; provided, however, that: (i) the center obtains documentation of authorization from the individual patient; or (ii) waiver of individual authorization has been approved by either an institutional review board or privacy board.          (e) The center may disclose de-identified health information of an individual for the purposes of lowering total medical expenses, coordinating care, benchmarking, quality analysis, research, administrative or planning purposes, informing consumer health care decisions or other purposes that aim to improve healthcare or public health outcomes for commonwealth residents that are consistent with the goals of this chapter.
